Lattice is primary synchrotron single-crystal data at 295 K. Bulk modulus is adiabatic (Brillouin). Debye temperature: ELASTIC (acoustic), DERIVED BY ME, NOT A QUOTED VALUE. materials.notes: °C converted to K by +273.15. Lattice: neutron powder data 'at room temperature' (exact T not given in CIF) so T_K=null. Bulk modulus: large scatter in literature for monoclinic ZrO2 (the authors say their EOS differs from previous high-pressure experiments but is comparable to Brillouin values); ±28 GPa. Thermal expansion values are DERIVED by me as interval means [dL/L0(T2)-dL/L0(T1)]/(T2-T1) from TPRC axial dL/L0 tables (%, ref 293 K), assigned to interval midpoints, restricted to T <= 1200 K because of pretransformation anomalies (930-1100 °C per Patil & Subbarao) and the m->t transition; TPRC marks axial values PROVISIONAL and the non-monotonic a-axis values (dip near 850 K) reflect data scatter. Directions are monoclinic lattice-parameter axes, not tensor principal axes. TPRC tabulated polycrystalline alpha (direct values): 8.8 (293), 7.6 (400), 7.1 (500), 6.7 (600), 6.5 (700), 6.4 (800), 6.4 (900), 6.9 (1000), 7.5 (1100), 8.9 (1200) x1e-6/K - the decrease with T is characteristic of microcracked polycrystals and should not be used as an intrinsic value. Cross-check: Patil & Subbarao (1969) abstract give mean axial coefficients for monoclinic ZrO2 a = 10.31, b = 1.35, c = 14.68 x1e-6/°C (mean over their measured range). Modern tensor data (Haggerty et al. 2014, doi:10.1111/jace.12975) could not be opened - recommended upgrade. TPRC figure gives 'M.P. 2963 K' vs Hong et al. 2018 2710 °C (2983 K). Debye temperature: CALORIMETRIC, but from a Debye-model fit to C_p measured over 150-823 K, not a low-temperature (T -> 0) limit. Source: Degueldre, Tissot, Lartigue & Pouchon, 'Specific heat capacity and Debye temperature of zirconia and its solid solution', Thermochimica Acta 403, 267-273 (2003). The abstract says 'zirconia' without naming the phase; undoped ZrO2 at 150-823 K is in the monoclinic stability field (m->t begins near 1200 K per Patil & Subbarao), so I take it as monoclinic, but this is my inference. Doped solid solutions give 575-625 K in the same paper. A true low-T calorimetric study exists (Nevitt, Fang & Chan, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 73, 2502 (1990), C_p of monoclinic ZrO2 at 2.75-350 K), but its abstract gives no Debye temperature and the full text is paywalled. That paper reports excess low-T heat capacity from low-lying optic modes, so a low-T-limit theta_D could differ substantially from 590 K. Treat this value as uncertain at the ~10-20% level.

materials.notes: 1 dyn/cm^2 = 0.1 Pa, so 1e12 dyn/cm^2 = 100 GPa. Lattice: room-temperature value; exact T not stated in the CIF, so T_K=null. Thermal expansion alpha read directly from TPRC recommended table (polycrystalline/cubic, 'iso'; referred to L(293 K)); TPRC marks only T<=250 K values as provisional. Debye temperature: CALORIMETRIC (low-T C_p fit, single crystal). Value 515 ± 20 K is from McCalla, Gastiasoro, Cassuto, Fernandes & Leighton (arXiv:1808.03909). They state it is 'in excellent agreement with recent single crystal work', and it matches Ahrens et al., Physica B 393, 239 (2007): 513 K for an undoped single crystal (their Supplementary Table SI). Range: the same table lists undoped SrTiO3 values of 324 K (Henning & Hegenbarth 1984, single crystal), 428 K (Duran et al. 2008, polycrystal) and 513 K (Ahrens 2007). The text says the scatter for undoped SrTiO3 'spans from 324 to 513 K'; including doped samples it spans 235-534 K. Melting point: congruent melting from DTA, Tf = 2079 ± 20 °C = 2352 ± 20 K (Guguschev, Klimm, Langhans, Galazka, Kok, Juda & Uecker, 'Top-seeded solution growth of SrTiO3 crystals and phase diagram studies in the SrO-TiO2 system', CrystEngComm 2014 / arXiv:1310.2117). It was calibrated against the Al2O3 melting point taken as 2054 °C. Bulk modulus is DERIVED by me from the quoted Cij; adiabatic.
